sources.title: Ted Jacobson, Introduction to Quantum Fields in Curved Spacetime and the Hawking Effect, complete lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 59-page PDF retrieved; §§6.2.1–6.2.2, printed pp. 32–38, equations (6.1)–(6.26), read in full for the outgoing packet, horizon split, exponential relation, thermal factor and greybody coefficient.

contents.name: Collapse setup, incoming state and outgoing packet decomposition
contents.support: The notes formulate a free scalar on a fixed collapsing Schwarzschild background, use late outgoing positive-Killing-frequency packets, and split the backwards-propagated packet into reflected and transmitted pieces. Their additional local free-fall vacuum discussion is source context; the item separately states its own Hadamard, incoming-ground and operator-norm convergence assumptions.

contents.name: Near-horizon exponential redshift and greybody-filtered number
contents.support: The notes analytically continue the logarithmic near-horizon packet, compute the negative-frequency norm, and obtain a Bose factor multiplied by the transmitted packet norm identified as the greybody probability. The item's finite-band integral and ordered packet-concentration limit are proved from its explicit direct-integral model premise; the source's narrow-band approximation is not treated as a uniform finite-packet error bound.

sources.title: Stefan Hollands and Robert M. Wald, Quantum fields in curved spacetime, complete review
sources.locator: Complete 77-page PDF retrieved; §2.3(c), PDF pp. 26–31, equations (52)–(60), read in full for state distinctions, collapse assumptions, localized two-point pairing and late-time packet occupation.

contents.name: Hadamard, incoming-ground and settled Schwarzschild hypotheses
contents.support: The review states the collapse result for a Hadamard state approaching the ground state at spatial infinity and a future domain that is exactly Schwarzschild; it localizes the late packet two-point function near the horizon and suppresses the infinity contribution. The item's operator-norm convergence on each fixed band is an additional explicit model premise, not attributed to the review.

contents.name: Normalized late packet number and greybody factor
contents.support: Equation (56) gives the late-time occupation $|D_\ell(\nu)|^2/(e^{2\pi\nu/\kappa}-1)$ for normalized sharply peaked packets. The local theorem derives its stated integral and ordered limit under the adopted direct-integral convergence rather than claiming the review supplies a finite-band uniform bound.

sources.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes
sources.locator: Complete 46-page PDF retrieved; §3, PDF pp. 10–13, read in full for the fixed-background collapse calculation, exterior-only scope and temperature convention.

contents.name: Collapse calculation on a classical background
contents.support: The review describes a free quantum field on a classical collapse geometry, computes late-time particle content at infinity, and explicitly notes that the argument uses the exterior field region without Einstein field equations. The item retains a fixed background and makes no coupled-gravity claim.

contents.name: Hawking spectral scale and scope distinction
contents.support: The review states $T=\kappa/(2\pi)$ in natural units and distinguishes collapse radiation from equilibrium and Unruh settings. The item converts the spectral parameter to SI dimensions directly and does not claim an observed temperature.

sources.title: Stefan Hollands and Robert M. Wald, Quantum fields in curved spacetime, complete review
sources.locator: Complete 77-page PDF retrieved; §2.3(c), PDF pp. 26–31, equations (52)–(60), read in full for state distinctions, collapse assumptions, localized two-point pairing and late-time packet occupation.

contents.name: Boulware, Unruh and Hartle-Hawking state distinctions
contents.support: The review distinguishes the exterior Boulware ground state, collapse/Unruh incoming-ground and outgoing-thermal conditions, and the two-sided regular Hartle-Hawking equilibrium state. The remark preserves their different domains and boundary conditions and makes no Kerr existence claim.

sources.title: Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes
sources.locator: Complete 46-page PDF retrieved; §3, PDF pp. 10–13, read in full for the fixed-background collapse calculation, exterior-only scope and temperature convention.

contents.name: Collapse radiation versus equilibrium settings
contents.support: Section 3 treats collapse radiation and the equilibrium/Unruh settings as distinct physical constructions. The remark uses this only as a scope distinction; it asserts no state-existence result for Kerr.
